newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP to quit Hunter Valley coal - paper.
newsitem.headline: BHP to quit Hunter Valley coal - paper.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd plans to quit its A$185 million investment in the Hunter Valley as part of what could be the company's total exit from the thermal coal market, The Australian Financial Review reported on Friday.
"The decision to sell the Mount Owen open cut mine just eight months after its commissioning comes amid BHP's new hard-nosed review of its assets," the newspaper said.
It said BHP Coal had given Centaurus Corporate Finance the mandate to sell the mine, which it said had underperformed because of a difficult geological structure.

"It is understood the decision to dispose of Mount Owen is part of a corporate push to return to BHP's core coking coal business, where returns are much higher than thermal coal and where the company sees its strength," the newspaper said.

"BHP has ruled that any assets giving an internal rate of return of less than eight percent will be sold and businesses that return between eight and 12 percent will be reviewed for possible sale," it said. "Only those returning 15 percent can be certain of being kept."

The newspaper said other thermal coal assets, including the Moura mines and Blackwater mines in Queensland and BHP's three mines in Indonesia, also were under review by consultants McKinsey and Associates and may also be offered for sale.
BHP's thermal mines produce about 15.3 million tonnes a year for export markets, generating revenue of about A$700 million.
